government.note: One-party state led by the Workers' Party of Korea (WPK), with two subordinate allied parties. Real power lies with the supreme leader, who heads the WPK and the top state military body (Kim Jong Il: Chairman of the National Defence Commission from 9 April 1993 and WPK General Secretary from 8 October 1997; Kim Jong Un: First Chairman of the National Defence Commission from 2012, then Chairman, later styled President, of the State Affairs Commission from 29 June 2016). From 1998 to 2019 the President of the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly (later translated as Chairman of its Standing Committee) was the nominal head of state; the April and August 2019 constitutional amendments transferred the head-of-state powers to the Chairman of the State Affairs Commission, and the 2026 amendment moved the remaining power to receive foreign envoys' credentials to the same office. The schema allows only one head-of-state office, so the Standing Committee chair (the nominal head of state at the game start) is used throughout and the change is recorded here. The Supreme People's Assembly elects the Premier and the Standing Committee; the Constitution was last amended on 23 March 2026, when 'Socialist' was dropped from its title.

holders.note: Leader from the death of Kim Il Sung until his own death. Chairman of the National Defence Commission from 9 April 1993 and WPK General Secretary from 8 October 1997.

Leader from his father's death; first reported as supreme leader on 27 December 2011. WPK First Secretary from 11 April 2012, Chairman from 9 May 2016 and General Secretary from 10 January 2021; First Chairman of the National Defence Commission from 13 April 2012 (Wikidata) and Chairman/President of the State Affairs Commission from 29 June 2016.

offices.note: Informal title for the de facto leader, who holds the WPK's top post and the top state military post. It is not a constitutional office; 'party_congress' is used for selection because the WPK congresses and conferences confer the party title.

system.note: 687 single-member constituencies with one approved candidate on each ballot, nominated through the Democratic Front for the Reunification of Korea (dissolved 23 March 2024); official turnout is above 99%. A 2023 amendment to the election law provides for fielding more than one candidate (Yonhap, cited by Wikipedia); the 2026 SPA election still had one candidate per constituency. The 14th SPA's term ran past its five years: the 15th SPA was elected on 15 March 2026, not in 2024 as expected. seats_2000 is the result of the 26 July 1998 election (10th SPA, in office on 1 January 2000); 'others' are the 7 deputies of Chongryon, the pro-North association of Koreans in Japan.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Estimate only. North Korea has no competitive elections and single-candidate ballots, so there is no vote share to derive from. The weights are a gameplay estimate: most support goes to the WPK's official line (Juche, modelled as marxist_leninist because no Juche sub-ideology exists), a large share to the military-first (Songun) emphasis of the late 1990s (statist), and small shares to market-oriented reform sentiment and to the two subordinate allied parties (the Korean Social Democratic Party and the Chondoist Chongu Party, which together held 76 of 687 seats).
